difficultyRationale: Tests the classic fragile-base-class problem: recognizing that patching individual overridden methods is a symptom-level fix, while switching to delegation addresses the root cause.
prompt: A codebase has `class EventLoggingList<T> extends ArrayList<T>` which overrides add(T) to log every addition, so that logging is reused wherever a List is needed. A bug is later found: calling addAll(Collection) on an EventLoggingList does not log anything, because ArrayList's internal addAll implementation does not call the overridden add() for each element. What change best fixes the root design problem, not just this one bug?
explanation: The root problem is that EventLoggingList depends on undocumented details of how ArrayList's own methods call each other internally — a classic fragile base class issue. Switching to composition (a private List<T> delegate wrapped by a class that implements the List interface, adding logging only at the specific methods that actually add elements) decouples the logging behavior from ArrayList's internals, which is exactly the approach the JDK's own Collections wrapper implementations (e.g., Collections.synchronizedList) use to add behavior to a collection without subclassing it.

options.text: Switch to composition: have EventLoggingList hold a private List<T> delegate and implement the List interface by forwarding calls to it, inserting logging only at the methods that actually add elements (add, addAll) — this decouples the logging behavior from ArrayList's internal implementation details.
options.explanation: By delegating instead of inheriting, the logging class controls every entry point itself rather than depending on which internal method ArrayList happens to call; this is the same decorator-style approach the JDK uses for its own collection wrappers, such as Collections.synchronizedList.

options.text: Override addAll() too, and keep extending ArrayList, patching each List method individually as further logging gaps are discovered.
options.explanation: This treats each gap as a one-off bug rather than the underlying cause: any future ArrayList method that adds elements through some other internal path can reintroduce the same silent gap, so the fix never actually closes.

options.text: Make EventLoggingList final so that no further overriding-related subclassing bugs can occur, on the theory that preventing anyone from creating a further subclass of EventLoggingList removes the risk of silently bypassed overrides anywhere in the hierarchy, including in third-party code that depends on this list implementation.
options.explanation: Marking the class final only prevents further subclassing of EventLoggingList itself; it does nothing about the existing bug, since addAll() still bypasses the overridden add() regardless of whether EventLoggingList can be extended further.

options.text: Remove logging entirely, since the inheritance relationship with ArrayList is otherwise valid and should not be disturbed.
options.explanation: This abandons the actual requirement (logging every addition) instead of fixing the design that fails to meet it, and it ignores that the inheritance relationship itself is what caused the silent gap in the first place.
